manualReview.summary: Seventy-two-hour fasting effect reconstructs from author tables
manualReview.note: The authors deposited Fed-versus-24h and 24h-versus-72h edgeR tables rather than a direct Fed-versus-72h table. Algebraically combining their log2 fold changes yields the registered 72h-minus-fed effect: 15,326 genes join, Pearson=0.99995, median absolute delta=0.0286, and all 3,564 strong effects agree in sign. P values and FDR cannot be reconstructed from separately fitted adjacent contrasts. GSE294478 shares the exact title and contributors of Ferris et al., Science 2025 (PMID 40743333, PMC12434793); the paper's data statement cites BioProject PRJNA1238491 but does not list GSE294478 among its GEO accessions. The authors' sequential RNA-seq comparisons do not include fed vs 72-h fasted directly, so the registered fasted72h_vs_fed contrast is a re-analysis, not an author contrast. The paper's main text gives only 'n=3-4' for the bulk RNA-seq heatmap (Fig. 1C) and does not say whether each library is one mouse; GEO gives no sex or animal field for the bulk libraries. The adult female CLAMS physiology cohort (n = 10) and snRNA-seq cohort (n = 3 per state) are separate experiments and are not transferred. The reviewed crosswalk from registered CTRL_CV/3CR_CV columns to RNAseq_Ctrl/RNAseq_3CR libraries is an alias interpretation, not a published animal-ID table. The Science supplement (not open access; not retrieved) and the bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2024.06.26.600891 remain to be checked for per-library animal and sex statements.
